## Overview

ROCKET AF (ClinicalTrials.gov number NCT00403767) randomly assigned 14,264 patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation at increased risk for stroke to [rivaroxaban](./rivaroxaban.md) 20 mg daily or dose-adjusted [warfarin](./warfarin.md). The per-protocol, as-treated primary analysis tested noninferiority for the primary end point of stroke or systemic embolism ([src_8ff4bad2e9d926335b4de77ad1e41630](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_8ff4bad2e9d926335b4de77ad1e41630.md)).

## Reported results

The primary end point occurred at 1.7% per year with rivaroxaban and 2.2% per year with warfarin in the primary analysis (hazard ratio 0.79; 95% CI 0.66 to 0.96; P<0.001 for noninferiority). Major and nonmajor clinically relevant bleeding occurred at 14.9% and 14.5% per year respectively, with significant reductions in intracranial hemorrhage and fatal bleeding in the rivaroxaban group ([src_8ff4bad2e9d926335b4de77ad1e41630](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_8ff4bad2e9d926335b4de77ad1e41630.md)).

The trial was funded by Johnson & Johnson and [Bayer](./bayer.md) and is one of the four trials pooled in the meta-analysis of new oral anticoagulants ([src_8ff4bad2e9d926335b4de77ad1e41630](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_8ff4bad2e9d926335b4de77ad1e41630.md), [src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63.md)).
